headline: Football — 1925 season
summary: The 1926 yearbook recounts the 1925 team's unbeaten, unscored-upon run to the Adirondack Interscholastic League title: 180 points for, none against, including an 82-0 rout of Port Henry in a drenching rain and a title-clinching 26-0 win at Plattsburgh.
copyright_basis: Public domain in the US (published before 1931) — yearbook text as transcribed on the Historic Saranac Lake Wiki
full_text: After two years of bitter struggle our football team surpassed even the fondest hopes of its supporters, in this, the third year of its gridiron activities, by winning the championship of the Adirondack Interscholastic League, and marching through the season without defeat and with uncrossed goal line. The season's total score was one hundred and eighty points. — The season started with a victory over our ancient rival, Lake Placid H. S. We easily won the next game from the weak team representing the Lake Placid Club School, the score being 41 to 0. Then on a muddy and greasy field, in a drenching cold rain, we crushed the formidable warriors from Port Henry. They towered above us and the odds seemed in their favor; but when they dug the mud out of their eyes, they read: "Saranac Lake, 82; Port Henry, 0." The team in midseason form won from Tupper Lake the hardest game of the season the score being 12 to 0. The championship was clinched by winning the final game from Plattsburg by 26 to 0. — This was the most successful athletic season in the history of S. L. H. S. and credit must be given to the squad and to Mr. Kenneth Wilson whose able coaching, resulting from his athletic experience was a great factor in achieving this success.

headline: Wallace to stay in Saranac Lake
summary: Three-sport star Tom Wallace dropped plans to move to California and returned for his senior year; the story recaps his state hurdles record and calls him a power on the gridiron for three seasons.
copyright_basis: Public domain in the US (published before 1931)
full_text:
SARANAC LAKE, June 16 — Tom Wallace, regarded as one of the greatest athletic stars developed at the high school, will not be lost to the institution this year. A change in plans made to go to California will keep him in the local school. He will complete his junior year this month and enter his senior year next September.

Wallace has been a consistent star on not only the track and football field throughout his high school well. He jumped center on last winter's basketball team and in no small measure it was his playing that made a championship contender of the local five.

As captain of the track team this season Wallace led his teammates to victory over Malone in a dual meet here and the championship of the Adirondack interscholastic league at Tupper Lake. He was the only member of the team to qualify in the sectional at Canton to go to the state meet last Saturday at Ithaca. There he lowered a state record he made last year in the 220-yard low hurdles altho, because of a tie with another track man from Rochester and a wind favoring the runners, his last year's mark, will stand for another year.

Wallace has been a power on the football gridiron for three seasons. He had a great year in football last year and was one of the most feared men by the schools that faced him.

paper: Canaras (SLHS yearbook), 1930 — scan on the HSL wiki
headline: Football 1929
summary: The 1930 yearbook calls 1929 the high point of the program's first seven years: a fifth straight Adirondack League title and a 6-6 tie with Franklin Academy; 5-1-2, with the only loss to Northwood School.
copyright_basis: Public domain in the US (published before 1931)
full_text:
Football reached the highest point of its seven year career at Saranac Lake High School during the season of 1929, when the Red and White gridmen not only won their fifth consecutive Adirondack League championship but went on to tie for the mythical supremacy of Northern New York by holding Franklin Academy of Malone to a 6-6 deadlock. Incidentally, this was the first time in four years that a Saranac eleven has not succumbed to the powerful Green and White teams from the North.

Graduation will be unusually severe with the Red and White squad as only two of the first string men will be on hand for practice next fall. Besides "Walt" Finnegan, erstwhile leader of the 1929 aggregation, "Bob" Downs, "Joe" Beiderbecke, "Bill" Hopkins, Harris Ryan, "Chuck" Bowker, "Wally" Herron, "Tag" Tagliabue and "Mil" Deitz will receive their diplomas this June. Captain-elect "Bud" Malone and "Ed." Plummer, alone of the regular eleven will return for 1930.

THE SEASON'S RECORD — S.L.H.S. 25, Canton H.S. 6; S.L.H.S. 18, Lowville Academy 0; S.L.H.S. 6, Tupper Lake H.S. 6; S.L.H.S. 12, Lake Placid H.S. 7; S.L.H.S. 19, Plattsburgh H.S. 0; S.L.H.S. 13, Tupper Lake H.S. 7; S.L.H.S. 0, Northwood School 39; S.L.H.S. 6, Franklin Academy 6. S.L.H.S. 99, Opponents 71. Won 5, Lost 1, Tied 2.
